title: Personal Checking: Electronic-Transaction Disputes, Notice Windows and Provisional Credit Timing
content:
## Which debits can be disputed

A Personal Checking electronic-transaction dispute is a claim the owner brings about a debit made by debit card (at home or abroad), at an ATM (PCB's own, another bank's in the United States, or abroad), by ACH debit or by Zelle. Paid checks, wires and official checks do not go through this process. A claim is registered as a dispute in submitted status, with its notice date set to the day the owner told PCB of the error.

## Notice window

The owner's notice qualifies only if it reaches PCB within the tier's notice window, in calendar days, from the posting of the disputed debit. The day after the posting date is day 1; the notice qualifies when the notice date is no later than the posting date plus the window, the last day included. Both dates are read from the records.

## When a provisional credit is owed

A provisional credit becomes owed on a dispute that is still in submitted status once the tier's provisional credit deadline, in business days, has run from the notice date.

- Only weekdays count as business days, and a weekday that is a Federal Reserve holiday does not.
- The first business day after the notice date is day 1 of the count.
- The credit is owed on any date that is on or after the business day on which the count is completed.
- Where the account had been open fewer calendar days than the tier's new-account period on the notice date, the tier's new-account deadline takes the place of the ordinary one.

Only a dispute in submitted status can receive a provisional credit, and no dispute receives more than one.

## After the investigation

- **Resolved in PCB's favour, or withdrawn.** The provisional credit may then be reversed, in its full amount, through a reversal that names the provisional credit entry. No reversal is possible while the dispute stands in any other status.
- **Resolved in the owner's favour.** The provisional credit becomes permanent without any new entry, and every overdraft item fee whose source is the disputed debit is refunded, with the refund reason recorded as a final dispute outcome.

## Retired clause

The general sizing clause that used to set a provisional credit at the owner's claimed sum, never above the disputed debit, is **no longer in force**; provisional credits are now sized under the Personal Checking sizing basis that took its place.

## Counting illustration (hypothetical)

Notice is given on a Friday, and no Federal Reserve holiday falls in the weeks that follow. The Monday after is day 1. With a hypothetical deadline of 3 business days, the count completes on the Wednesday: the credit is owed from that Wednesday onward, and on the Tuesday it is still not owed. The weekend in between adds nothing to the count.

Notice window, on the boundary: a notice dated exactly the posting date plus the window qualifies; a notice one calendar day later does not.

superseded_clauses: The provisional credit amount is the dispute's claimed_amount, but never more than the disputed item's amount.
